finCouple.r1_d: Your answers do not describe a relationship coming to an end. Something may have worried you enough to bring you here, but it does not show up in the facts: you see each other, you picture a future, your circle is still shared, and separation is not on the table.
finCouple.r1_a: If you came this far, something crossed your mind. Say it, simply, without turning it into a heavy conversation. It is far easier now than in six months.
finCouple.r2_d: There is a real slowdown, and you did not invent it. But the essentials hold: you talk, you touch, you still picture a future. What your answers describe is a relationship running at low revs, not one that is ending.
finCouple.r2_a: Pick up one habit you had lost, just one, and keep it for three weeks. A dinner with no screens, an outing on Saturday. Couples are not saved by grand declarations.
finCouple.r3_t: You have entered the lukewarm zone
finCouple.r3_d: Nothing serious has happened, and that is exactly the problem. Your answers describe a relationship that works without being fed any more: fewer gestures, fewer plans, evenings that all look alike. At this stage it does not hurt, it wears you down.
finCouple.r3_a: The lukewarm zone can last for years, and that is where the danger lies: nobody decides anything, and one day it is too late. Put a word on it out loud this week.
finCouple.r4_t: The relationship holds, but not much is feeding it
finCouple.r4_d: What you describe is no longer a rough patch. The signals add up: everyday life has emptied out, plans have gone, the people around you are quietly splitting into two camps. Your relationship is held up by what was built before, not by what is happening now.
finCouple.r4_a: Ask yourself one question and answer it honestly: what changed first, and when? There is almost always a precise moment. Finding it is worth more than ten conversations circling around it.
finCouple.r5_t: The relationship has emptied out, and you know it
finCouple.r5_d: Your answers leave little room for doubt. This is no longer an impression, these are facts: you tell each other nothing, the gestures have gone, so have the plans, and one of you has already started to pull away. You are not making a drama out of nothing.
finCouple.r5_a: Do not waste time wondering whether you are exaggerating, you are not. The real question is whether you want to try to repair it, and whether both of you want that. One person is not enough.
finCouple.r6_t: You are at the end of the relationship, even if nothing has been said
finCouple.r6_d: Almost everything that makes a couple has disappeared from your answers. What is often left is a shared organisation and an address. The word separation has already come up, or one of you is seriously thinking about it. This is not a crisis, it is an ending in progress.
finCouple.r6_a: The worst outcome at this stage is letting another year slip by hoping it comes back on its own. Set yourself a deadline, in your own head: the date by which you have the real conversation.
finCouple.r7_d: Your answers describe two people who share little more than an address or a habit. No plans, no gestures, no confidences, no desire, and a six-month projection that shows you apart. The relationship is finished, it simply has not been declared yet.
finCouple.r7_a: This is no longer about saving something, it is about choosing how it ends. That choice is still yours, and it is the only one left.
finCouple.r8_t: The break-up has already happened, only the date is missing
finCouple.r8_d: There is no interpreting this score. Everything you answered points the same way: the relationship ended a while ago, and what is holding it together has nothing to do with the couple any more. Fear, logistics, money and children are real reasons to stay, but they are not reasons to love.
finCouple.r8_a: You do not need a test to know what is going on, you already know. Talk to someone this week, someone real, not a search engine.
